consensus_findings: Across lanes, FY2025 keeps Tesla's manufacturing, demand, and regulatory backbone but pushes autonomy and AI capability closer to the center of the filing.
All lanes identify Robotaxi, Cybercab, Bot commercialization, and autonomy dependence as the clearest forward-looking additions to the risk story.
Multiple lanes agree that FY2025 adds more immediate 2025 trade-policy and incentive-roll-back language, including tariffs, retaliatory pricing effects, and repeal risk.
The broad change is better read as a platform-roadmap and policy-shock pivot than as a generic AI rewrite.
disagreement_findings: P2 is the clearest first read because it most explicitly ties policy shock to cost, demand, and commercialization exposure.
P1 stays useful on the same evidence packet, but it reads more like a broad autonomy and execution pivot than a tighter mechanism chain.
P0 catches the overall autonomy turn, but it is less disciplined about the specific policy and commercialization needles that make the case vivid.
why_this_case_matters: TSLA belongs in the public casebook because it teaches how external pressure can re-center a filing. The value is not just that autonomy appears more often; the value is that trade policy, incentives, and commercialization dependence change the first question the workflow should ask.
investor_read: The practical shift is from a mainly EV-manufacturing and demand story toward a business that now sounds more dependent on autonomy, Robotaxi, Cybercab, Bot, and AI capacity, while also absorbing immediate tariff and incentive shocks. The investor question is whether the filing now asks you to read Tesla as a commercialization-and-policy case rather than just an execution case.
protocol_read: Methodologically, this is a strong case because the same tagged packet can support a sharper or blurrier first read. P2 best exposes the mechanism chain, P1 remains useful but broader, and P0 shows what a simpler control does to specificity and stop discipline.
caveat: This remains a paragraph-packet case view. It supports a public judgment about answer shape and bounded mechanism, but it does not prove a full-filing benchmark result or justify shipping outline compare in this pass.
